issues.legal_issue: An increase in the size of a project beyond the scope of its existing environmental clearance constitutes an expansion requiring environmental appraisal even when the project remains within the schedule’s upper threshold.
material_facts: The project received an environmental clearance for a construction area of 32,395.17 square metres.
The construction area was later increased to 40,480.88 square metres, still below the schedule’s upper threshold of 1,50,000 square metres.
The increase exceeded the area covered by the existing clearance.
issues.conclusion: The increase was an expansion requiring the procedure for a fresh environmental appraisal, notwithstanding that the project remained within the schedule’s upper threshold.
issues.legal_principle: Paragraph 7(ii) of the 2006 EIA Notification requires an application and appraisal when an expansion increases a project beyond the capacity for which prior environmental clearance was granted; unlike paragraph 2(ii), it does not require that the expansion cross a further schedule threshold. Read as a whole and in light of the Notification’s environmental-protection purpose and the precautionary principle, the Notification does not permit a project proponent to increase a cleared project incrementally without appraisal. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: environmental_clearance_expansion_case and prior_clearance_granted and increase_exceeds_cleared_scope and increase_within_schedule_ceiling

predicates.environmental_clearance_expansion_case: The case concerns an increase to a project that is subject to environmental-clearance requirements.
predicates.prior_clearance_granted: The project proponent received environmental clearance for the project before the proposed increase.
predicates.increase_exceeds_cleared_scope: The proposed increase enlarges the project beyond the scope covered by its existing clearance.
predicates.increase_within_schedule_ceiling: After the increase, the project remains within the applicable schedule ceiling.
predicates.fresh_environmental_appraisal_required: The project proponent must obtain appraisal of the increased project through the applicable environmental-clearance procedure.

issues.definition: When a project with prior clearance is enlarged beyond the cleared scope, remaining within the applicable schedule ceiling does not remove the requirement for appraisal.

issues.legal_issue: An environmental authority cannot validly approve an expansion by amending an existing clearance without following the prescribed application and appraisal procedure.
material_facts: The project proponent sought an amendment after increasing the construction area beyond the area covered by the existing clearance.
The project proponent did not submit an updated Form 1.
The environmental authority granted an amendment without processing the proposal through the relevant expert appraisal committee.
The amendment recorded the increased area but did not assess its potential environmental impact.
issues.conclusion: The authority could not grant the amendment without following the procedure for appraisal of an expansion; the amended clearance was therefore not validly granted.
issues.legal_principle: Paragraph 7(ii) of the 2006 EIA Notification prescribes the procedure for applications seeking clearance for an expansion, including appraisal by the relevant Expert Appraisal Committee or State Level Expert Appraisal Committee and a decision on the due diligence required. The prescribed procedure must be followed rather than replaced with an amendment that bypasses appraisal. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: environmental_clearance_amendment_case and authority_granted_amendment and increase_exceeds_cleared_scope and required_appraisal_bypassed

predicates.environmental_clearance_amendment_case: The case concerns an authority’s amendment of an existing environmental clearance after a project was enlarged.
predicates.authority_granted_amendment: The environmental authority approved the enlargement by issuing an amendment to the existing clearance.
predicates.increase_exceeds_cleared_scope: The enlargement went beyond the project scope covered by the existing clearance.
predicates.required_appraisal_bypassed: The proposal was not submitted through the prescribed application and appraisal process before approval.
predicates.amended_clearance_invalid: The amendment does not validly approve the enlargement.

issues.definition: An amendment approving an enlargement beyond the cleared scope is invalid when the authority grants it without the prescribed appraisal.

issues.legal_issue: When construction has been completed without the required environmental appraisal, remedial environmental assessment and measures may be ordered, including compensatory exaction.
material_facts: Construction of the expanded project was complete by the time of the tribunal’s order.
The expansion had not undergone the prescribed appraisal of its environmental impact.
The tribunal directed a monetary deposit and appointed an expert committee to evaluate the project’s impact and suggest remedial measures.
The Supreme Court directed the committee to continue its evaluation and suggest compensatory exaction.
issues.conclusion: The Court upheld the tribunal’s directions, including the deposit and the expert committee’s work, and directed the committee to continue assessing the project’s impact and suggest compensatory exaction.
issues.legal_principle: A core tenet of the EIA Notification is that construction should not proceed until sufficient scientific evidence has been gathered to understand the project’s environmental impact. Once construction is complete and prior evaluation has been denied, the available response is to assess the impact and take remedial measures. The Court relied on the Notification’s environmental-protection purpose and precautionary approach; it cited no earlier cases for this conclusion.

predicates.appeal_against_environmental_tribunal_or: The case is an appeal from an environmental tribunal’s order concerning a project’s environmental compliance.
predicates.construction_completed: The project proponent completed construction before the environmental impact of the relevant expansion was evaluated.
predicates.required_environmental_appraisal_not_per: The project’s expansion did not undergo the required environmental appraisal before construction was completed.
predicates.post_construction_remedial_directions_up: The Court upholds directions for environmental assessment and remedial measures after construction is complete.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns a project completed without required environmental appraisal, the Court upholds directions for post-construction assessment and remediation.
